business_scope.primary_industry_name: Light Value-Added Postponement Packaging and Custom Kitting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Arab Republic of Egypt — unitary national incorporation regime, no sub-state corporate registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — civil law system rooted in the Napoleonic Code, with Islamic Sharia recognized as the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Constitution, and with pragmatic court and tribunal practice accommodating common-law contractual drafting for foreign investment vehicles.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Arab Republic of Egypt and the United States of America (in force 1986)
Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreement between Egypt and the European Union (in force 2004)
Agreement on Promotion, Protection and Guarantee of Investments among Arab States (in force 1980)
Egypt–United Kingdom Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement
Egypt–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (in force 1982)
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS — Egypt participating member since 2016

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Laws No. 36/2014, No. 154/2019 and No. 8/2024, together with its binding Executive Regulations; Law No. 8 of 2015 on the Registration of Terrorist Entities and Terrorists; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Article 87, and GAFI implementing circulars on beneficial-owner disclosure schedules in incorporation filings; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1999 on corporate record-keeping; FRA Board Decree No. 117 of 2023 on Beneficial Owner Registers for non-banking financial entities; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT instructions applicable to the LLC's capital and operating bank accounts.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or official Trade Register Extract of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or authorized registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., state Secretary of State or national Companies House equivalent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Active Status of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Same competent company registry as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of each foreign shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC, approving the draft Articles of Association, and designating the signatories of the incorporation file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and notary public of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation counsel or resident representative to execute incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's jurisdiction (with proficiency in English/Arabic)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national ID of each UBO, accompanied by a certified Arabic translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national ID issuing authority of the UBO's country of residence; certified translation by a translator registered under Law No. 145 of 1944

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or entity profile confirmation for each foreign shareholder and each UBO, evidencing banking identity due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance department or relationship manager of the shareholder's or UBO's depositary bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Binding and mandatory before incorporation for each direct shareholder and each UBO against: (1) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (2) the U.S. OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists; (3) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (4) the Egyptian national terrorist list maintained under Law No. 8 of 2015; and (5) PEP screening to FATF Recommendations 12 and 24 standards as implemented by EG-FIU guidance, covering domestic and foreign PEPs, their immediate family members and close associates; plus (6) adverse-media and negative-news review in Arabic and English. Risk-based enhanced due diligence on source of wealth and source of funds applies where any PEP or high-risk jurisdiction nexus is identified. Given the Low_Risk_Standard tier of ISIC 5210 fulfillment/kitting, a standard customer due diligence file, biannual re-screening for new PEP status, and mandatory suspicious-transaction reporting to the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit will apply.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI National Investment Portal and the electronic Commercial Registry (Sijill al-Tijari) operated by the Ministry of Justice; submission via https://businessportal.gov.eg or GAFI investor service centers, with name clearance executed through the integrated 'name check' procedure against the Commercial Registry records and the Egyptian Trademark Office database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name must be registered in Arabic; the Latin-script name of the company is registered as a transliteration and may be referenced in brackets within the trade name line. The Arabic name must include the LLC legal-form suffix 'Dhat Mas'uliyya Mahduda' (شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة). Latin-only names are not acceptable for the Commercial Registry. Transliteration must follow the phonetic standardization used under Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1999 rules, avoiding deceptive similarity with existing Arabic or transliterated English names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / بنك (any banking connotation — Central Bank of Egypt approval required)
Insurance / تأمين (all financial-sector connotations — Financial Regulatory Authority pre-approval required)
Petroleum / بترول and Gas / غاز (Ministry of Petroleum approval required)
Egypt / مصر / Misr (limited to majority-Egyptian-owned entities or with prior approval to prevent implied state affiliation)
Arab / العربية (requires substantiated pan-Arab or League of Arab States licensing nexus)
International / الدولية, Global / العالمية, United / المتحدة (requires documentary proof of multi-jurisdiction operations)
National / الوطنية and State / للدولة (reserved exclusively for public-sector or state-controlled institutions)
Military / عسكري, Presidential / رئاسي, Ministry / وزارة, Government / حكومي (absolutely prohibited without sovereign decree)
Central / المركزي (reserved for monetary and public supervisory authorities)
Group / مجموعة (requires evidence of an affiliate group structure registered in Egypt)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 47 of 2018 (Limited Liability Company provisions, Articles 36-62); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Civil Code notarization requirements for Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for incorporation and Commercial Registry clearance; Commercial Registry Directorate of the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (E'tabnamah / Memorandum of Association) accompanied by GAFI Incorporation Application Form No. 1 and Commercial Registry Request Form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital under Law 159/1981; the capital must be fully subscribed by quota-holders and adequate for the licensed activity. If contributed in cash, the amount must be deposited into a provisional Egyptian bank account and evidenced by a bank certificate; in-kind contributions require a certified accountant's valuation report. Non-resident quota contributions may be remitted in foreign currency through licensed Egyptian banks.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the submission of the Articles of Association dated [DATE] is ratified and the quota subscription of the initial shareholders, representing 100% of the issued capital, is hereby approved and accepted. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [City, Egypt] and the legal address is to be recorded with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and the Commercial Registry. RESOLVED, that [SOLE MANAGER] is appointed Sole Manager (Chairman) and the following officers are appointed: [CEO], [CFO], and [Company Secretary], each vested with banking and statutory authorization. RESOLVED, that the authorized officers execute and file commercial store licenses under Law 164/1960, tax registrations, and all ancillary administrative matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Form Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official name reservation request designating a limited liability company and provide three alternative Arabic trade names with English transliterations. Verify that the intended activity of warehousing, light assembly and custom kitting conforms to ISIC 5210. The name reservation certificate is valid for 30 days and must not conflict with existing registered trademarks or prior company registrations.
required_dossiers: Copies of national ID or passport of each incorporator
Signed power of attorney or authorization of the legal representative
Three alternative trade names in Arabic with English transliterations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, file a re-application with revised names within 3 business days; if contested against an identical registered name, submit an escalation letter to the GAFI Internal Review Committee together with trademark search evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office (Tawtheeq) in conjunction with a licensed corporate law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in Arabic in compliance with Law 159/1981, specifying the LLC legal form, capital division into quota units, management structure, duration, transfer restrictions and registered office. All incorporators must execute the deed before the Notary Public; foreign incorporators acting by power of attorney must have the power of attorney notarized and legalized by the Egyptian consulate in their jurisdiction.
required_dossiers: Drafted Articles of Association in Arabic
Certified power of attorney if execution is by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary Public refuses certification, amend the clauses conflicting with mandatory provisions of Law 159/1981 and re-present the revised deed within 5 business days together with the notary's written observations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Provisional Bank Account and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian bank such as the National Bank of Egypt or Banque Misr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate bank account in the name of the company and deposit the declared share capital, obtaining an official bank deposit certificate. If contributions are made in kind, engage a certified public accountant (Muraqib El-Hesabat) to issue a valuation report attesting to the fair value of each in-kind quota contribution. The provisional account remains restricted until the GAFI incorporation certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Provisional incorporation letter issued by GAFI
Passport or national ID copies of quota-holders
Certificate from licensed accountant for in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the deposit due to AML/KYC concerns, obtain a non-objection letter from GAFI confirming the legal form and apply to an alternative licensed bank with supplementary corporate ownership documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registry Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (OSS) and Commercial Registry Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Association, bank certificate, incorporation application and lease documents at the GAFI OSS. The OSS consolidates the registration with the Commercial Registry (Sijel Togari), issues the commercial register certificate, tax card, social insurance number and activity codes in a single workflow. The company obtains separate legal personality on the date of successful Commercial Registry registration.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or title deed for the registered office
Copy of national ID or passport of all incorporators and appointed directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The OSS serves a 15-day curing notice for any missing or defective documents; if the dossier is closed after 30 days of inactivity, a new application must be filed with additional administrative fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card, VAT and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the consolidated tax card (Bitaqah Darbiyah) covering income tax file creation and simultaneously apply for value added tax registration under Law 67 of 2016 if annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000. Register all employees with NOSI within 14 days of commencement and open the workforce file under Law 79 of 1975.
required_dossiers: Social insurance Forms 1 and 2 for insured persons and workplace
Copy of manager and authorized signatories' identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA delays issuance, request a temporary numbering receipt to enable lawful invoicing; for VAT or social insurance assessment disputes, file a grievance with the taxpayers' unit or NOSI appeals committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commercial Establishment License and Post-Registration Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Administrative Unit (Al-Hayy) and Governorate Commercial Licenses Committee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the commercial store license (Rukhset Mahal Tugari) under Law 164 of 1960, attaching the civil defense fire safety certificate, structure clearance, lease title and site manager identification. Undergo a final civil defense inspection and obtain the district's license before commencing warehouse or kitting operations. Maintain Arabic signage, opening-hours permits and capacity limits as directed by the license conditions.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or ownership deed of the warehouse
Proof of occupational health and safety measures
Identification documents of the site manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district refuses issuance, file an administrative appeal with the Governor's Appeals Committee within 15 days; resolve all civil defense observations and request a re-inspection before the appeal deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade, Commercial Licensing Directorate; Governorate District Unit (Al-Hayy) Commercial Licenses Committee
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Store Operating License (Rukhsat al-Mahal al-Tujari) for Warehousing, Light Assembly and Custom Kitting under Law No. 164 of 1960

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (registration): light warehousing, kitting and assembly operations with limited environmental footprint require streamlined Form C environmental assessment and registration protocol under Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009; a full Environmental Impact Assessment report (Category A or B) is not mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2000 for wastewater discharge to public sewer (pH 6.5-9.0, BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L); air emissions and VOC thresholds per Law No. 4 of 1994 and its Executive Regulations; hazardous waste handling and transfer under Waste Management Regulation Law No. 202 of 2020; noise limits of 55 dB(A) daytime and 45 dB(A) night-time in mixed residential-industrial zones per Ministerial Decree No. 459 of 2007.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Directorate certification confirming fire suppression systems, emergency exits, alarm and smoke detection equipment, fire extinguisher placement and evacuation planning in accordance with the Fire Protection Code; engineering administration structural load inspection and building safety certificate; occupational health and workplace clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 and Ministerial Decree No. 211 of 2003, covering first aid readiness, accident prevention, personal protective equipment and employee training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity intending to make taxable supplies in Egypt must appoint an Egyptian tax representative, who is jointly and severally liable for VAT obligations. The representative files the VAT registration application with the competent ETA office via the unified electronic portal, attaching the entity's constitutional/power-of-attorney documents, certified incorporation instruments, and the tax representative's legal identification. Upon verification, ETA issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the entity is registered for VAT under Law No. 67 of 2016. The same TIN is used for withholding tax, payroll tax, and e-invoicing enrollment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian tax law does not provide check-the-box or general hybrid-mismatch elections. An Egyptian LLC is per se a taxable resident juridical person subject to entity-level corporate tax under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 as unified by Law No. 26 of 2020. No elective pass-through status exists for an LLC. Group filing may be available only where expressly permitted under the tax law; hybrid mismatch treatments are not elective and are constrained by general anti-avoidance rules and transfer pricing substance requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and its executive regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration when annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000; persons making zero-rated export supplies may register voluntarily regardless of turnover, and other below-threshold businesses may optionally register if they perform taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates electronic invoicing and e-receipts for VAT-registered taxpayers on a phased basis. Invoices must be issued through ETA-certified systems, transmitted to the ETA portal near real time via secure API integration, validated by ETA, and printed with a machine-readable QR code. No physical fiscal stamping is used; digital validation by ETA serves as fiscal clearance. Non-compliance triggers fines under the VAT Law and underlying executive regulations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Egypt to outside the customs territory are zero-rated provided the export is completed and evidenced within the period prescribed by ETA. Services rendered to non-residents qualify for zero-rating when supplied for direct use and benefit outside Egypt, subject to documentary evidence of offshore consumption and receipt of foreign currency. The zero-rating applies only to genuine exports; domestic supplies of goods and services remain taxable at the standard rate absent a specific statutory exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate / proof of foreign currency repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA may audit export files retroactively and deny or claw back zero-rated VAT, refunds, and credits where documentation is defective or where the purported export is found to be fraudulent. Penalties include a VAT shortfall assessment of 100% of the due tax, additional monetary fines escalating with the period of non-payment, interruption of e-invoicing clearance, and suspension of tax certificates. Criminal liability, including imprisonment, may attach to submitting forged customs or foreign-inflow documentation under the VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 and customs legislation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE; Arabic: البنك المركزي المصري) acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 on the Central Bank and the Banking System, being the sole monetary authority, regulator of all FX transactions, and supervisor of licensed banks; co-regulators for treasury flows are GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) for FDI registration and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) for profit-remittance tax clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP operates under a CBE-managed flexible market-determined exchange-rate regime (unified rate since March 2024) with no official parity; current-account transactions for genuine trade and services are broadly convertible, but every FX operation must be intermediated by a CBE-licensed bank and evidenced by underlying commercial documentation (contracts, invoices, and, for goods, the ACI/ACID customs declaration via NAFEZA). Capital-account convertibility remains restricted: inward equity injections and outward profit remittances require GAFI registration, bank intermediation, and full tax compliance, and non-resident shareholders face a domestic 10% dividend withholding tax (treaty reduction available) plus presentation of audited financial statements, a valid tax card, and an ETA tax-clearance certificate. The post-2024 flexible regime has essentially removed explicit FX rationing, but each remittance is still subject to bank-level compliance review of 3-10 business days, and mismatched purpose codes or undocumentary flows can trigger CBE penalties, administrative fines, and CIT adjustments under Law 194/2020.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion of hard-currency export receipts into EGP is currently imposed; EG_LLC may retain 100% of proceeds from goods export or cross-border fulfillment/kitting services in USD or EUR accounts at an authorized Egyptian bank. The statutory repatriation obligation requires all such proceeds to be credited to the LLC's account with a CBE-licensed bank within 180 days from the bill-of-lading date or service-completion date, supported by the underlying sales/fulfillment contract, commercial invoices, customs/ACI declarations, and bank credit advice. Failure to repatriate or unjustified delays must be explained to the bank and the CBE and may expose the unrepatriated balance to 22.5% corporate income tax adjustment risk and administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (formation-stage collection) / Operational EGP and USD Accounts
Capital Escrow Account (formation-stage collection) / Operational EGP and USD Accounts
Operational EGP and USD Accounts with corporate internet banking and trade-finance desk
Operational EGP, USD and EUR Accounts with dedicated trade desk
Premium Operational Package (EGP/USD) with HSBC global connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary or regulated settlement rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Wise, Payoneer) hold no CBE banking licence, cannot open a domestic Egyptian account, cannot settle in EGP, and cannot lawfully collect Egyptian trade receivables under Law 194/2020, which channels all deposit-taking, FX execution, and payment clearing through CBE-licensed banks. EMIs remain viable only as supplementary non-resident wallets for disbursing non-EGP vendor payments (software, freight, marketing) from offshore funds; every compliant inbound receipt and EGP-denominated obligation must clear through the licensed Egyptian bank, and EMI statements should be retained merely as payment evidence rather than as regulatory KYC documents.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or bank-supervised live-video presence is effectively mandatory. Standard CBE AML/CFT practice requires the Ultimate Beneficial Owners (each holding 25% or more), managers, and authorized signatories to attend an in-person or bank-verified video KYC interview; pure remote opening is not accepted by NBE and Banque Misr, while CIB and QNB may accept a hybrid model consisting of a remote UBO interview plus a locally notarized power of attorney appointing a resident authorized signatory. Foreign directors should arrange an apostilled power of attorney and should budget 2-4 weeks for corporate extract verification, Arabic/English document legalization, sanctions screening, and final compliance committee approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or layered indirect ownership obscuring the natural-person UBO at the 25% threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current shareholders register showing the full chain of ownership to natural persons; GAFI-stamped incorporation pack; notarized UBO declaration per CBE AML Rulebook; certified passports and proof-of-address for each UBO; organizational chart and board resolution confirming absence of bearer or nominee shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or managers without Egyptian residency while requesting high limits and full internet banking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled power of attorney appointing a resident general manager; local commercial registration extract naming the resident agent; national ID and residence permit of the local signatory; board resolution limiting signing mandates; recorded two-way video KYC interview and certified passport copies of all foreign directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the inward capital injection from an offshore parent or third-country holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements of the remitting entity; audited statutory accounts of the parent; share-subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; underlying dividend, sale, or divestment documentation supporting lawful origin of funds; tax identification numbers and registered-office proof of the remitter; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hits, or payment routing through high-risk jurisdictions (UAE, Cyprus, Russia-linked counterparties).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions-screening explanations with SWIFT correspondent logical-path justification; counterparty KYC files (licences, passports, bank references); warehousing, inventory, and kitting sub-contracts proving economic substance; external legal opinion confirming non-application of OFAC/EU/UN lists; board minutes rationalizing the transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Declared warehousing and kitting profile inconsistent with unusually high transaction velocity or cash-intensive counterparties, suggesting trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed 3PL and fulfillment agreements with actual principals; warehouse lease contracts; pick-list and kitting bill-of-materials records; customer invoices with proof-of-delivery orders; insurance policies on stock; internal audit reports and the completed AML risk-rating questionnaire confirming the Low_Risk_Standard tier.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) before remittance, EG_LLC opens a non-operational capital-collection account at the chosen CBE-licensed bank using its incorporation pack; (2) the foreign shareholder issues an English/Arabic board or shareholder resolution stating the exact USD or EGP amount, share allocation, and GAFI registration number; (3) the remitter executes a SWIFT MT103 from its own corporate account with a strict beneficiary reference of 'EG_LLC share capital subscription - GAFI No. [XXXX]' and the CBE inward-transfer purpose code for direct investment/capital contribution; (4) the receiving bank verifies the GAFI commercial registration, articles of association, passports, and tax card, credits the capital account, and reports the inflow to the CBE through its electronic reporting platform; (5) funds are released to the operational account only after commercial and tax registration are conclusive. No prior CBE approval is required for standard FDI inflow, but the bank may request a source-of-wealth declaration for transfers above approximately USD 1 million; all MT103 confirmations, purpose-code annotations, and bank credit advices must be retained as treasury audit evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import settlements (packaging materials, kitting machinery, inventory) the LLC must first obtain an ACI/ACID declaration number through the NAFEZA single window before shipment; banks will then execute either a commercial letter of credit (preferred for large capex), documentary collection, or direct SWIFT MT103 with underlying invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and insurance certificate attached, with no blanket LC mandate post-2024. For non-import service payments (freight, software, third-country subcontracting), the rail is SWIFT MT103/202 with contracts and invoices, subject to ETA withholding tax (up to 20% on service and royalty fees or applicable treaty relief) and to the 10% dividend withholding tax on profit distributions to non-residents. Domestic EGP operating payments (wages, rent, utilities, local suppliers) should use the CBE Egypt ACH (EG-ACH) direct-credit rails; Airwallex-type EMIs may be used only for premium-conversion non-EGP vendor payments and are expressly excluded as the onshore settlement rail for Egyptian receivables.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore FX forward (USD/EGP, EUR/EGP, etc.) for documented trade and fulfillment exposures, maturities typically up to 12 months, requiring underlying LC, invoice, or purchase-order support and 10-20% initial margin.
FX swap (spot-forward combination) for short-term EGP liquidity management across month-end, tax, and payroll cycles.
Cross-currency swap among USD/EGP notional for multi-year asset or equipment financing, subject to CBE-licensed bank approval and documented exposure.
FX options (structured strategies such as collars) to hedge contingent foreign-currency exposures, permitted only with bank-approved option strategies and real trade documentation.

Offshore NDFs (USD/EGP non-deliverable forwards) are generally inaccessible to resident non-bank corporates; they are available mainly through international bank windows for portfolio investors and are not recommended for EG_LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 120) with audited financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year end (30 April for a 31 December year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of EGP 5,000-50,000, monthly delay interest at CBE discount rate + 2% on unpaid tax, enforced collection, and criminal liability for the responsible manager.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements with General Assembly approval, filed at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), registration desk
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year end (30 June for a 31 December year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers face fines under Companies Law 159/1981 (up to EGP 50,000), suspension of GAFI approvals, and restrictions on onward registry transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Consolidated Payroll and Withholding Tax Statement (Form 6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), regional WHT office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EGP 500-5,000 per-offense fine, interest on withheld amounts, and potential disallowance of wage deductions in the CIT assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Confirmation and AML Register Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI e-Government platform and Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) AML supervision unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the GAFI annual filing (within 30 days of the ordinary general assembly); within 14 days after any qualifying share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EGP 1,000,000 under AML Law 80/2002, with criminal exposure for directors and compliance officers who conceal real ownership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration Renewal (quinquennial event reported annually in the compliance calendar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office (Ministry of Trade and Industry) via GAFI counters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every 5 years from the anniversary of the commercial registration certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late surcharges; lapsed registration bars new tax cards, banking facilities, and import activity; prolonged lapse leads to administrative strike-off and judicial dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for every Egyptian LLC irrespective of size or turnover; no small-company exemption under Companies Law 159/1981. Auditor must be an ESAA-licensed chartered accountant registered with the Financial Regulatory Authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS; IFRS directly required for entities under Financial Regulatory Authority supervision.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO declarations are filed at incorporation and re-confirmed annually with the general-assembly financial statements; changes of 25% or more of ownership or any new controlling person must be filed with the Commercial Registry and reflected in the UBO register within 14 days of transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger with transfers)
Minute Book of Ordinary and Extraordinary General Assemblies
UBO Register maintained under AML Law 80/2002

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 1,000 per annum (serviced registered office with mail handling and statutory-notice capacity in Greater Cairo or Alexandria)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - 3,500 per annum (ESAA mid-tier firm, private LLC with 1-10 employees and standard warehousing/kitting operations)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt applies a flat 22.5% corporate income tax on resident companies and on non-resident permanent establishments deriving Egyptian-source income. The Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits a 50% deduction from taxable income for up to five years for qualifying projects in designated governorates and Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) investment areas. Fulfilment/kitting businesses operating in licensed free zones may elect the free-zone regime, which replaces corporate income tax with an annual customs-based charge on the value of goods exiting the zone. Export-oriented kitting and assembly activities are also entitled to VAT-zero-rating and customs duty exemptions for imported raw/input materials under the Export Goods regime, but such exemptions do not automatically eliminate CIT unless the free-zone election is obtained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the Egypt Tax Authority (ETA) E-Tax portal at https://eservice.eta.gov.eg; transfer pricing disclosure schedules are attached to the same electronic return when applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; taxpayers are also required to file preliminary quarterly CIT declarations and make quarterly advance tax payments during the fiscal year, reconciled against the annual Form No. 100 within the annual filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form No. 100 must be submitted no later than four months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the statutory deadline is 30 April of the following year. Quarterly advance payments are due by the last day of the month following each calendar quarter, and the fourth quarter payment must accompany the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Tax Identification and Registration Data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax card number, commercial registration number, fiscal year start and end dates, and entity legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian tax identification number of the permanent establishment or branch; enter the foreign entity's foreign tax ID only as supplementary data. Non-resident companies without a PE must complete this box using their Egyptian residency registration if any; otherwise they should file the non-resident withholding tax return rather than Form No. 100.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales, service fees, and incidental revenues from fulfilment, kitting, assembly, and packaging activities, including export revenues and any free-zone sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egyptian-source gross revenues. For a permanent establishment, include all revenues attributable to the Egyptian branch irrespective of the contract's governing law. Intercompany billings must be reported at book value in the currency of the audited financial statements, with EGP equivalent disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Sales and Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases, subcontract labour, packaging materials, rent, wages, utilities, depreciation, and overhead directly attributable to kitting/assembly operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expense deductions for a non-resident PE are allowed only for costs incurred for and reasonably attributable to the Egyptian business. Intra-group charges must satisfy arm's length standards under the Egyptian Transfer Pricing rules; royalty or management fee cross-charges to the PE must be excluded or disclosed separately. Keep original vendor invoices, customs declarations, and payroll records available for ETA inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Controlled Transactions / Transfer Pricing Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value of related-party purchases, sales, service fees, royalties, interest, and other cross-border or domestic controlled transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors must attach the Egyptian Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form if the aggregate controlled transactions exceed the statutory threshold (EGP 10,000,000). State the methodology applied (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split) and the functional, asset, and risk profile of the kitting/assembly PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result after adjusting accounting profit for tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses, prior-year losses carried forward (up to five years), and any free-zone or investment-law deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report taxable income attributable to the PE in accordance with the treaty business profits article. If claiming a loss, annex a tax loss reconciliation and preserve all records to justify future carry-forward. The loss carry-forward period is five years and is not available if the entity lacks economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Liability and Advance Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at 22.5% on taxable income, less quarterly advance payments previously made, withholding tax credits, and any final settlement amount due or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders filing through an Egyptian PE must also declare any profit repatriation in the related withholding schedules; dividends or branch remittances are not deductible from CIT but may trigger the 10% dividend withholding tax under domestic law. Attach the treaty relief application when reduced WHT is claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form No. 100 triggers an administrative late-filing surcharge plus delay tax of 2% per month or part month on the unpaid tax, capped at 20% of the tax due. Additional fixed fines for failure to submit books, records, or the transfer pricing disclosure form are assessed by ETA at its discretion. Wilful failure to file or submitting a false return is treated as tax evasion and leads to criminal prosecution, confiscation, and director-level liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividend distributions made by an Egyptian LLC to its shareholders, including non-resident shareholders, under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended. This withholding tax represents the final tax on distributed profits and is withheld by the Egyptian company at the time of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced withholding rate under an Egypt income tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of which it is fiscally resident for the relevant calendar year. The TRC must be legalised/apostilled and accompanied by a certified Arabic translation if requested. The Egyptian paying company must file a treaty relief application with the ETA before the dividend resolution date, or the non-resident shareholder must file a refund claim after withholding. The application must identify the ultimate beneficial owner, the shareholding percentage, and the treaty article. The ETA may deny relief where the shareholder does not have substantive ownership, substance in its country of residence, or the arrangement is considered an artificial conduit.

cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht.domestic_statutory_rates: Egyptian domestic WHT for non-resident royalties and interest is 20%; the rate for technical, management, and administration service fees paid to non-residents is likewise 20%. These domestic rates apply unless a tax treaty provides a lower rate.
cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht.treaty_reference: Egypt's income tax treaties generally reduce royalty and interest withholding to rates between 5% and 15% for a beneficial owner that is subject to tax in its state of residence and meets the possessive conditions of the relevant treaty article. The ETA requires a TRC and an anti-abuse/beneficial-ownership submission to grant treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 aggregate related-party controlled transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory contemporaneous Local File documentation. A Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds EGP 500,000,000, and Country-by-Country Reporting is triggered when the group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 800,000,000 (or the EQE comparable threshold of EUR 750,000,000). The documentation must be retained and supplied to the ETA within 30 days of a formal request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the UAE/GCC Economic Substance Regulations, but Egyptian law and the ETA articulate a strong substance-over-form doctrine. A fulfilment/kitting LLC must evidence real premises, employees carrying out assembly/kitting operations, inventory management, and decision-making capacity. The ETA may disregard a legal entity transaction or recharacterise an arrangement under Law No. 91 of 2005 Article 30 if the entity has no economic substance, is purely interposed between the foreign investor and the Egyptian activity, or functions as a conduit for treaty shopping.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppression of cash or ACH/Airwallex receipts, issuing forged invoices, under-reporting inventory, recording fictional costs, or presenting misleading accounts to the ETA to reduce the 22.5% CIT liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the full underpaid tax, delay surcharge of 2% per month capped at 20%, additional administrative penalties, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion. Courts may impose imprisonment, confiscation of equipment and bank balances, and fines equal to the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who sign false returns or direct the evasion may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes. They face personal civil restitution, travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment under the Egyptian Income Tax Law and Penal Code. Directors cannot hide behind the LLC's limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an Egyptian LLC with no staff, no physical warehouse, no assembly/kitting equipment, and no business risk; routing profits through a shell foreign parent or sister company solely to access the Egypt-Cyprus or other treaty benefits and dilute Egyptian taxation through artificial intra-group fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may disregard the corporate entity or recharacterise the transaction under the substance-over-form doctrine, deny treaty withholding relief, and assess tax at 22.5% on the reattributed Egyptian-source income along with late-payment surcharges and transfer pricing penalties. The entity may also be struck off the commercial register and denied free-zone or investment-law incentirates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally assessed for the full amount of tax avoided through sham entities; they may face a departure ban, prohibition from managing companies in Egypt for up to five years, and criminal liability if the arrangement is adjudicated as deliberate evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflated intercompany management fees, royalties, or finance charges paid from the Egyptian fulfilment/kitting entity to a foreign group company; setting an artificial low margin on kitting services to leave no taxable profit in Egypt; or failing to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation despite exceeding the EGP 10 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may adjust taxable income to arm's length, disallow excessive deductions, deny double tax relief, and apply a 22.5% tax on the upward adjustment plus 2% monthly delay surcharge and TP-specific penalties. Persistent violations may be referred to the ETA audit and dispute collection board.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's length agreements without economic/financial justification may be jointly liable for the TP adjustment amount, undergo criminal proceedings for fraudulent tax reduction, and be exposed to arrest warrants and seizure of personal assets where the adjustment exceeds the capacity of the company to pay.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using ACH Direct or Airwallex channels to receive payments for kitting/assembly services while invoicing them as pure logistics or warehousing to evade withholding tax or VAT; creating multiple bank accounts to split receipts; accepting undisclosed cash deposits to avoid ETA visibility. Although the sector is low-risk, deliberate opacity in payment documentation is red-flagged by banks and the Anti-Money Laundering Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of Egyptian AML Law No. 80 of 2002 carry fines up to EGP 10 million and imprisonment, separate from tax sanctions. The ETA may reopen closed tax assessments upon discovery of unreported payment rails, impose double withholding, and blacklist the entity from government licences and customs facilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are liable under AML law for knowingly using false invoices or payment descriptions. Personal sanctions include criminal imprisonment, director disqualification, freezing of bank accounts, and civil confiscation of amounts received through misclassified payment rails. The corporate veil is pierced when the payment system is used for money laundering.
